title: Cap Rate in Property
subtitle: Property Value = NOI / Cap Rate
openingQuestion: What does a cap rate tell you that matters most?
openingOptions: Whether rents are high or low against the market
NOI as a share of the property's value
How much leverage is on the asset
The vacancy rate of the space
explanation: Cap rate = NOI / property value. It is the unlevered yield on a property: if you bought it at today's market price, this is the annual return the rental income alone would give you, before any borrowing. It carries perceived risk as well as yield - a well-located, liquid asset trades at a lower cap rate, meaning a higher price for the same income, while a riskier one needs a higher cap rate to compensate.

realWorldExample.description: Two office buildings each produce net operating income of VND 10bn a year. The one downtown, let to large firms on long leases, is priced at a 6% cap rate - about VND 167bn. The one on the edge of the city, with higher vacancy and less stable tenants, trades at a 10% cap rate - VND 100bn. The same income stream, a gap of nearly 70% in value. So the cap rate is not a quality score where higher is better: it is the risk premium the market is demanding.

quiz.question: If the cap rate falls and NOI is unchanged, what happens to the property's value?
options: It falls by exactly the amount the cap rate fell
It rises, because the cap rate is the denominator
It is unchanged, because NOI is what sets the price
It falls, because a lower yield drags the price down
quiz.explanation: Value = NOI / cap rate, so the cap rate sits in the denominator and moves against the price: a lower rate raises the value. It does not fall by the same proportion the rate fell - the relationship is a division, not a subtraction - and NOI alone does not set the price, because the same income is worth different amounts at different required yields.

quiz.question: Why is the cap rate on a downtown office usually lower than on a suburban warehouse?
options: Because a suburban warehouse always has higher NOI than an office
Because cap rates are not applied to downtown property
Because the risk is lower, so investors accept a lower yield
Because the cap rate is worked out from the floor area
quiz.explanation: A cap rate carries both yield and perceived risk: a well-located, liquid, low-risk asset usually has a lower cap rate (a higher price for the same NOI); a riskier asset needs a higher cap rate to compensate.

quiz.question: Why does a low cap rate usually go with an asset seen as safer?
options: Because banks lend more against low cap rate assets
Because safe assets usually have high operating costs
Because a low cap rate means the asset's NOI is low
Because with lower risk, investors accept a lower yield
quiz.explanation: The cap rate is the required yield. The more certain the cash flow, the lower the yield investors accept - which means paying more for the same NOI.

quiz.question: Which of these does a cap rate NOT reflect?
options: The effect of borrowing to buy the asset
The yield the market requires on that asset
The relation between annual NOI and the asset's value
How risky the market perceives the asset to be
quiz.explanation: A cap rate is calculated as though the asset were bought outright in cash. Once there is debt, the return on your own equity is amplified in both directions and has to be worked out separately.

quiz.question: Two buildings have the same net income; one downtown at a 6% cap rate, one suburban at 10%. Which is worth more?
options: The suburban one, because a higher cap rate means it earns better
The downtown one, because the same income over a lower rate gives a higher price
They are worth the same, because their net income is identical
You cannot compare without knowing the floor area and age of each
quiz.explanation: The cap rate sits in the denominator, so it moves against the price. A low rate reflects a market that treats the cash flow as more certain - good location, stable tenants - and will pay more for the same unit of income.

keyTakeaways: The cap rate is NOI divided by the property's value
A lower cap rate usually means a higher valuation
Only compare cap rates within the same property segment

practicePrompt.question: A commercial rental property has net operating income (NOI) of VND 10bn a year and a cap rate of 6.5%. What is the estimated property value?
options: About VND 153.8bn (Value = NOI / cap rate = 10bn / 6.5%)
About VND 65bn (using Value = NOI × cap rate)
About VND 100bn
It cannot be determined without the market land price
practicePrompt.explanation: The cap rate is the core valuation ratio in property investment. Value = NOI / cap rate = 10bn / 0.065 ≈ VND 153.85bn.

summary.keyIdea: The cap rate is NOI divided by the property's value
summary.commonMistake: Easy to miss: a lower cap rate usually means a higher valuation
summary.action: Only compare cap rates within the same property segment

application.title: In practice: cap rates in property
application.message: A commercial rental property has net operating income (NOI) of VND 10bn a year and a cap rate of 6.5%. What is the estimated property value?
application.secondary: Getting this principle solid lifts your professional financial analysis.

sections.text: In rental property investing, the cap rate is one of the first numbers an investor works out - and what it actually means is usually oversimplified.

The cap rate tells you the annual return from rental income if you bought the asset at today's market price, before any leverage. It carries more than yield: it also carries perceived risk. A well-located, liquid asset usually has a lower cap rate (a higher price for the same NOI), while a riskier asset needs a higher cap rate to compensate.

items: A falling cap rate with unchanged NOI pushes the value up (Value = NOI / cap rate)
Downtown property usually has a lower cap rate than the suburbs because the risk is lower
Cap rates only mean anything compared within the same property segment

sections.title: Three ways of writing the same formula

variables.name: Net operating income
variables.description: Rent collected less operating costs, management, property tax and insurance - before interest and depreciation.

variables.name: Capitalisation rate
variables.description: The yield the market requires for that asset type and level of risk.

example.title: Worked example
example.explanation: Four percentage points off the cap rate raises the value by 67% while the cash flow never moves. This is why, in property, a shift in market cap rates moves values harder than a shift in rents.

sections.text: Three things a cap rate does not tell you

items: Not leverage: a cap rate assumes a cash purchase. The actual return on your own equity is entirely different once there is debt.
Not the large capital spend coming: an older building about to replace its HVAC or lifts has a healthy NOI today and future cash flow that will be eaten into.
Not rent growth: two assets on the same cap rate are worth very different amounts long term if one sits where rents are rising fast.

sections.label: Be careful with the NOI you are handed
sections.text: The NOI in an offering memorandum is usually the optimised number: the highest occupancy ever achieved, thin operating cost estimates, and no property management fee. Rebuild NOI yourself from the actual leases and the last three years of costs before working out a cap rate.

lines: A low cap rate does not mean the asset is bad.
It usually means the market is pricing that asset as safer.
